findings.title: Ignored crypto providers are still instantiated and mutate global security state
findings.body: detectProvider streams the whole ServiceLoader before sorting, so every CryptoProvider on the classpath is constructed, not just the winner. DefaultCryptoProvider registers BouncyCastle with Security.addProvider and FIPS1402Provider inserts BCFIPS/BCJSSE at positions 1-3 and modifies security properties. Previously the multiple-provider case threw and aborted startup; now execution continues with the losing providers' global side effects still installed, which can pollute a FIPS deployment with a non-FIPS provider (or vice versa) while CryptoIntegration reports only the selected provider.

findings.title: Equal order() values make provider selection classpath-order dependent
findings.body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order() 200. When any two of them are present, the reversed sort leaves their relative order to ServiceLoader/classpath enumeration order, which is not a defined contract, and the previous explicit 'multiple providers' failure is gone. The JVM can therefore silently start with e.g. the Elytron provider (whose getBouncyCastleProvider() returns null) instead of the default/FIPS provider depending on jar ordering.

findings.title: New abstract order() method breaks all external CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: order() is added as an abstract interface method rather than a default method. Any CryptoProvider implementation outside the four updated in-tree classes will fail to compile against this version, and already-compiled implementations will throw AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration sorts providers by CryptoProvider::order. A default order (e.g. 100) would let existing implementations keep working.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns an unrelated JCA provider
findings.body: The method contract is to return the BouncyCastle (or BCFIPS) provider, but this implementation returns the provider of the default KeyStore type (e.g. SunJSSE/SUN for PKCS12). Callers that use the returned provider by name/capability for signatures, key factories or certificate handling will silently get a non-BC provider with different algorithms and behaviour, instead of an honest null (as WildFlyElytronProvider returns) or an unsupported-operation signal.

findings.title: ECDSA test uses one P-256 key pair for ES384/ES512 and never verifies a signature
findings.body: The constructor generates a single default (P-256) EC key pair, yet testES384 and testES512 pass it with signature lengths of 96 and 132 bytes, so the conversions are exercised on zero-padded/truncated values rather than real P-384/P-521 signatures. The only assertion is that asn1derToConcatenatedRS and concatenatedRSToASN1DER round-trip to the same bytes; swapped or otherwise invalid R/S encodings would also pass. The test should generate a key pair per named curve and verify the DER-encoded result with Signature.verify against the public key.
